{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested:
#   -q gpuvolta
#   -P e14
#   -l ncpus=12
#   -l ngpus=1
#   -l mem=96GB
#   -l jobfs=1GB
#   -l walltime=24:00:00
#   -l storage=gdata/e14+scratch/e14
#   -l wd
#   -M z5131023@unsw.edu.au

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  -c 12 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=24h \
  --queue=gpuvolta \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: PBS -P e14 (project/allocation) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: PBS mem=96GB has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: PBS jobfs=1GB (local job filesystem/scratch) has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: you may not get fast local scratch; I/O may be slower if it falls back to network filesystems.

# NOTE: PBS storage=gdata/e14+scratch/e14 (filesystem project quotas/permissions) has no portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: none directly for performance, but the job may fail to access required filesystems or quotas.

# NOTE: PBS -l wd (execute in submission directory) cannot be replicated portably here; we cd explicitly instead.

# NOTE: PBS -M (email) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive job emails.

cd /g/data/e14/jb2381/CabbelingExperiments/

# Julia
export JULIA_DEPOT_PATH="/home/561/jb2381/.julia"
export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=auto
module load julia

# PBS used $PBS_JOBID for log naming; approximate with Flux job id.
julia --project isothermal_gpu_salinitynoise.jl > ${FLUX_JOB_ID}.log
'
"
}
